reasons: Step 0 is clean: the special and each of its nine parts has a retell and a turn or a feeling. The cut test finds one line and no part: ruling-stands, which both final reviewers also found and which stands as written on the project manager's reading of the owner's "go ahead".

Every gate passes. Eight have nothing to judge or little, because no real account or post is in it. A3 passes on the owner's outline, which asks Larry to explain what old thinkers thought. A6 passes on the owner's ruling "Keep the rabbi" for religion and on this review for everything else. A13 is on record (61 items, all fresh from both reviewers) and nothing the staging or the sound added repeats an aired episode. A16 passes from the transcription: nothing heard is crude or offensive, and the lines about a real person that are still heard differently are listed and captioned.
Part B is 19 of 24. B11 is not applicable and is left out. The approval rule's 18 of 26 is 17 of 24 pro rata, and 19 clears both figures. No zero in B1, B2, B7, B8 or B12.

Rows at 1: B2 (it moves on the page and in the frames, but that rests on a voice nobody has heard in the mix, and its central sentence is heard as noise in all four takes), B7 (18 s of one profile shot on the street and 16 s of one close shot at the restaurant glass, the second with a lamp post behind his face), B8 (38 of 59 spoken lines are listed as heard differently, the three names among them; every one is in its caption as it is said), B9 (no chair sound, a burst of talk that cannot be cut off, seams in the room's bed under the owner's lines, and footsteps nobody has heard), B12 (the experiment is the whole episode and was built as set out, but both measures need three people watching with sound).

Rows scored for what they are for, because the owner set aside what they ask: B2 (does it move, does its lightness land), B3 (is what it rests on real and exact), B6 (affection, sincerity that is earned and not a speech, respect for the traditions), B9 (sound that is the place), B13 (range inside one piece).

Not heard and not watched in motion by this review. A16, B8 and B9 are scored from the fit report's heard text, the cue times and measured levels; B2 and B12 partly so. A8, A15 and B4 are scored from the 165 audit frames, the 12 credits frames and 14 frames shot for this review.

Addendum, 27 November 2026, after the owner's watch and four changes at the owner's word (the side street, no sliding bowls, Sibyl's look, a new start to the walk) and two sound fixes: the verdict stands and Part B is still 19 of 24, with no score changed. The figures above are of the cut as first reviewed. The scorecard's first addendum has the rows.

Second addendum, 27 November 2026, evening, after the owner added a fourth idea (one line of the Hávamál on the last block, in four new lines) and the sound editor made the room under the last lines one unbroken bed and cured "bad": the verdict stands and Part B is still 19 of 24, with no score changed. The cut is now 263.2 s with 427 spoken words in 64 lines; the record holds 66 items, all fresh; 40 of 64 spoken lines are listed as heard differently; the credits name two quoted translations. I agree with both gate reviewers that the fourth idea earns its place, that it costs the door its surprise, and that it brings the close nearer the two aired endings without being their mechanism. Check, verify and on-record pass. No stage audit covers this cut; I shot 51 frames of it. The scorecard's second addendum has the rows.
forTheOwner: This list was brought up to date on the evening of 27 November 2026, after the fourth idea went in. Times are from the cut as it now stands, 263.2 s (4:23). The record does not say that you have watched this cut; the one you called solid had three ideas.

New. Listen first to "Just me and one line from an old Norse poem.", 177.3 to 180.3. The sound editor asks for your ear on it too. As kept it is heard as "Trust me, find one line from an over-and-horse poem". Two other spellings of it were heard as something crude and were thrown out. If you hear anything of the kind, it should go back.

New. Listen to the quotation, "Rich did I feel when a comrade I found", 181.2 to 184.1. "Comrade" is heard as "camera" in three takes of four, and "Rich" is lost in one. It is a real translation and it is exact in the caption.

New. Listen to "Mostly.", 188.5. It is one word on its own beat, and the tool cannot make it out at all. The writer and the sound editor both say it may have to rejoin "That's the poem talking." (186.2). The pause before it is the point of keeping it apart.

New. Listen from "Nearly there. I usually walk this block on my own." (172.9) through "Just me", the poem and "Mostly." to "They'll have started without me." (195.4) and "There's an old Tamil book" (199.4). Three lines in about twenty seconds have him by himself, and two old texts fall inside twenty. Both gate reviewers pass it as one man with a tell, and so do I. If it plays as coyness, or as a man sorry for himself, that is where it will show.

New. What the fourth idea does to the door and the close, which both gate reviewers set out and I agree with. The door is no longer where we find out that he wants us to come; it is where he is caught at it a second time, and "So you see my position." (211.4) is funnier for it. And the close is nearer your two aired endings than it was: he is alone with one small thing of his own forty seconds before "Nobody has started." It is still a different mechanism. "They'll have started without me." is now the third line of his being alone, so that either-or weighs more than it did.

New. Watch the cut closer on him for the quotation (180.3) and back for the glance (184.1 to 185.9). The builder asks whether a cut is the right weight for the line. The glance now has to read as a man who has just heard himself.
New. The credits name the second translation. Its year, 1923, wraps to a line of its own.

New. Expect what people say Larry told them to move toward company. There are now two exact quotations in old English about forty seconds apart, and the second is the shorter and warmer. Three of the four old texts fall inside eighty seconds (133 to 211).

Settled since the last list: "bad" in "The good way and the bad way." is heard as "bad" in every take; "joke" is heard as itself; and the room no longer falls silent under "close". It is one unbroken bed now, at about the same level in every gap and for five seconds after "Goodnight."
Changed by that fix: your "It's a crazy mixed up world out there." (247.0) is a little less clear over the fuller room. Two takes of four were heard as "mixed up real loud there".

Article 3. Larry tells two old texts in his own words, quotes two more, and says what the rabbi meant. Your outline asks for that, and the gate passes on it. The reading that Article 3 and chapter 9 are about the people the show covers, and not long-dead thinkers, is still the project manager's reading and not your ruling.

"Keep the rabbi" is taken to cover the cook's story from the Zhuangzi and the couplet from the Tirukkural as well. That extension is the project manager's. The Norse line you chose yourself; its research card notes that the poem is sacred to some people living now, and the script does not name it aloud, name its speaker or draw anything for it.
"And the ruling stands!" (237.1) is still the one line the cut test finds, a sportscaster's shout 8.5 s before your table line. There is still no title card at the top.
"Same hour." (38.9), "Some nights." (55.6) and now "Mostly." (188.5): Larry ends several thoughts on a short dry phrase. It is his voice in this piece, and about where a rhythm starts to be noticed.
Listen to the hard question, "What if none of it ever gets put right?" (126.1). Since the start was rewritten it carries your "justice seems rare" alone, with only "the bad way" to point back to.

Listen to the rabbi's sentence, 139.8 to 145.2. The tool heard "It is not lied to it to compete to the work" twice and "It is not likely to complete the work" once; the second half is nearly right. It is exact only in the caption.

Listen to "One cook in back, feeding the whole room.", 62.1 to 64.8 (heard "One cook in bed, fitting the whole room", once "hitting the whole room"), and to "you don't eat while a guest stands outside.", 207.9 to 210.6, and "I had company.", 223.5 to 224.6, where "eat" and "had" were heard as "hit".

The names: Tarfon is heard as "Taran" (133.2), the Zhuangzi as "drwangza" (68.7), Tamil as "mil" and the Tirukkural as "Teragural" (199.4). "Rabbi" and "Torah" are heard as themselves. None is heard as an insult.

The engine cannot say "walk": "I like the rock home" (10.8), your "Would you lock with me a bit?" (14.2), "lock this black on my own" (172.9). Your other lines: "no short night" (3.5), "feel safe, closed" (250.1).

Three sounds: whether the two sets of footsteps (from 22.4, and alone under the poem at 181) sound like two people walking; whether the coin (102.7) is a coin and not the note the tune was missing; and the table's burst of talk (215.7), which cannot be cut off and trails under "You're late." There is no sound of a chair at 226.9.
The listening holds (52.2 to 53.8, 123.9 to 126.1, 195.4 to 197.4). He turns to us and nothing else moves. If they do not read as us speaking, the three questions he says back are rhetorical.

Why the door opens: a figure stands at the top window from 190.4 and is gone at 212.9, before the latch. And the look (224.6 to 226.5): six small heads turn to the camera. Cold viewers on stills missed both, and neither picture has been changed.
The bowl (232.3 to 234.1) is carried by a cut and his look, and "It's my house." (234.5) rests on it. Sibyl looks up at him for "It's still the rule." (235.7).

The cook's change of pace (84.5 to 91.3) at speed on a phone; Larry at the glass (64.8 to 81.0), where a lamp post stands behind the middle of his face; the street (22.4 to 56.4), which is one framing for 34 s; and the kerb, which is 50.6 s.

No stage audit has been run on this cut, and the audit's frames are still of the first one. I shot the last block, the door, the table, the end and the credits myself: the captions of the four new lines are exact, no word is on screen for the poem, and nothing printed a warning.

The experiment. Whether four earnest minutes in Larry's own words are a speech can only be answered by people who have not read it, watching with sound; both reviewers' measures ask three. You have watched twice and approved it.
Still open from your notes: how the archive lists a special.
